newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- South African financial markets rode a wave of optimism, lapping up the 200,000 rand individual allowance for offshore investment announced on Wednesday and revelling in a huge trade surplus in May after a surge in exports.
- A sharp hike in exports helped push South Africa's balance for May to a surplus of 1.75 billion rand, almost one billion rand higher than the previous month, customs and excise figures showed.

- A comprehensive job evaluation survey commissioned jointly by the government and public service unions has recommended yearly performance-related increases to about 85 percent of public servants who performed adequately.
- Black-controlled National Empowerment Corp and asset management company Coronation Holdings have announced the formation of an investment holding vehicle with a capital base of one billion rand.
- The Congress of South African Trade Unions would stage 24-hour strikes in each province from August 18 to 21 and two national strikes, possibly in September, it said.
- A report forming part of an assessment of the Cape Town 2004 Olympic bid says the Development Bank of Southern Africa's macroeconomic predictions for the games were off the mark.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The National Empowerment Corp and Coronation Holdings said they had joined forces to form an investment company called African Harvest, which will have a net asset value of one billion rand, including 800 million rand in cash.
- South Africa's larger television assemblers are furious about a proposal to slap a 20 percent duty on imported television tubes and maintain a 30 percent duty on imported sets.
- Group Five , the construction, engineering and building materials company, is to close down its loss-making property development division, chief executive Mike Lomas said.
- A surge in exports pushed the surplus on the trade account to 1.75 billion rand in May from April's 725 million rand.
- Consultation on the National Home Builders' Registration Council will begin with the publication of the draft new law on Friday, Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele said.
THE CITIZEN
- Gauteng Premier Tokyo Sexwale announced on Thursday he would step down as provincial premier in January 1998, to join the private sector.

- The Congress of South African Trade Unions announced a series of one-day strikes directed against the position of business on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, soon to be voted on by parliament.
- South Africa won praise from the markets on Thursday for its latest move to ease foreign exchange controls on individuals.
MAIL & GUARDIAN

- Members of the African National Congress (ANC) in Gauteng are furious with provincial premier Tokyo Sexwale for failing to consult them before deciding to quit politics for a position in the private sector.
- The ANC is embarking on a soul-searching, stocktaking campaign to pull itself together in the run-up to its December national congress.
--Johannesburg newsroom -27-11-482.1003
